basis: Cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss and skin atrophy/striae, each commonly >30% in overt Cushing syndrome; hypertension is separately coded.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinonasal disease and bronchiectasis (9/12); common ear damage is not established for this subtype.
Carcinoma originates in the urinary bladder, included in the renal axis.
Abnormal tract originates in the anal canal; associated cellulitis is a separately diagnosed infection.
Mucinous cystic neoplasm originates in extrahepatic bile ducts, included in the hepatic axis.
Developmental abnormalities of the anterior eye segment; extraocular features are not shared across most of this umbrella.
Inherited remnant lipoprotein disorder; atherosclerosis and fatty liver are separate diseases; xanthomas, corneal arcus and lipemia retinalis need not impair function.
Immune-mediated inflammation of cutaneous blood vessel walls defines the disease.
Inflammation is confined to the seminal vesicle, a reproductive organ; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not specified.
Lens opacity is explicitly attributed to diabetic hyperglycemia and disturbed glucose metabolism.
Hypertension remains uncontrolled despite multidrug therapy; renal and cardiac complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Bacteroides infection defines the concept; no anatomical site is specified or consistently affected across the group.
Primary biliary cholangitis is autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts; subtype designation does not establish other organ damage.
CoQ10 metabolic deficiency with encephaloneuropathy and deafness; valve regurgitation 2/2. Optic atrophy 2/2 omitted at cap; renal frequency uncertain.
Displacement of the lacrimal gland affects the ocular lacrimal apparatus.
Gastric mucosal disease defined by intraepithelial lymphocytes; associated coeliac disease or H. pylori infection is not implied.
Hereditary cerebral white matter degeneration causes dementia and motor dysfunction; hemianopia and abnormal breathing reflect CNS disease.
BRAT1-related neurodevelopmental disease with cerebellar atrophy and ataxia; nystagmus is neurologic and visual impairment is only 1-4%.
Thyroid hormone resistance commonly causes developmental impairment and skeletal dysplasia/delayed maturation (>30% each); constipation alone is not GI damage.
Cerebroretinal disease; fractures 8/12 and bleeding-prone GI telangiectasia 6/13 support involvement. Nail dystrophy 5/13 omitted at cap; anemia may reflect GI bleeding.
Ischemic necrosis directly damages bone; the varied underlying causes do not establish systemic vascular disease across the umbrella.
Spastic paraplegia from P5CS metabolic deficiency; muscle wasting and urinary incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than established primary muscle or urinary injury.
Panniculitis destroys subcutaneous fat, with lipoatrophy in 100%; localized fat loss does not establish systemic metabolic disease or a specific autoimmune mechanism.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss affects 8/8; motor delay in 2/8 is below threshold and does not establish neurologic damage.
IL-1 antagonist deficiency causes autoinflammatory sterile osteitis, periostitis and destructive pustular skin disease; pulmonary fibrosis occurs in only 1/9.
